request_id.description: Client-chosen correlation id (1-128 characters), echoed in the response.

protocol_version.description: Must be one of the supported protocol versions.

arguments.description: Operation arguments; may be omitted for operations without arguments.

request_id.description: The request's `request_id`, or null if it could not be read.

operation.description: The request's operation name, when it could be read.

revision.description:
Session revision after handling the request. It increases with every accepted
authoring mutation (including snapshot restores) and never decreases.

result.description: Typed result (see the operation's result schema). Present when `status` is `ok`.

oneOf.description: `result` is present.
`error` is present.

hint.description: Suggested recovery, when one is known.

ErrorCode.description: Stable error codes. Codes are never renamed within a protocol version.

The JSON is not a valid request envelope (missing, mistyped or unknown top-level fields).
protocol_version is not supported by this engine.
The request line exceeds the size limit.
No operation has this name.
Arguments do not match the operation's schema or are inconsistent.
This session's role may not perform the operation.
The operation needs an open project.
The project has no scene with this name.
A scene with this name already exists.
The scene has no entity with this id.
Names use 1-64 characters of a-z, 0-9, '_' or '-'.
The ASCII layout cannot be parsed.
Grid width and height must be between 1 and 64.
expected_revision does not match the current revision; nothing was changed.
A position (or move target) lies outside the grid.
The target cell already holds an entity.
A scene holds at most one player.
A scene holds at most one key per color.
Labels are 1-64 characters without control characters.
A rule parameter is out of range.
The scene lacks the required player/control or objective entities, so no episode can start.
The operation needs a started episode.
The episode already ended; start or reset one.
expected_episode_id is not the active episode; the action was not applied.
expected_tick does not match the episode's tick; the action was not applied.
A wall occupies the move target.
The move target is a door whose key the player does not hold.
No snapshot has this id in this session.
A documented limit (batch size, snapshot count, ...) would be exceeded.
A file could not be read or written.
The project file is malformed or violates scene invariants.
The replay file is malformed or its scene is invalid.
A file uses a format or hash version this engine does not support.
Engine bug. State changes commit only after a handler completes, so the request had no effect.

event or replay therefore denotes exactly one entity in that scene's history.

Role.description: Capability of a session, fixed by the launcher when the session is created.

oneOf.description:
Trusted: may create, inspect and modify projects, scenes and entities, run analysis,
snapshots and replay verification, and also play episodes.

Restricted: may only play episodes of the scene the launcher chose, observe them and
export their replays. Cannot change rules, spawn entities, set state or restore.

conventions: SI units: meters, seconds, kg, density kg/m2, impulse N.s, radians; Y points up.
Fully observable. Labels are authoring notes and excluded from player observations/replays.
Every accepted action advances exactly one fixed timestep; invalid actions change nothing.
request_id only correlates replies. Use expected_revision on author writes and expected_episode_id plus expected_tick on actions; after a lost reply observe before retrying.
Player capability is fixed by the launcher, bound to one saved scene; this is local separation, not remote authentication.
Scene editing is frozen while this host has a running episode; finish or forfeit first.
Goal overlaps are sampled at completed tick poses. Validation does not prove gameplay solvability.
Snapshot restore replays recorded inputs to rebuild solver caches, takes O(recorded ticks), increments revision and assigns a fresh episode ID.
Determinism is verified on macOS arm64 with the pinned toolchain/dependency set only; other platforms and versions are unverified.
